For `e = id + α·stopgrad(||id||)·normalize(t)`, detaching the norm removes the residual’s gradient through identity magnitude; identity still receives gradients through its additive path. Analytical implication: normalization gradients scale approximately as `1/||t||`, or `1/eps` below the clamp. Thus zero or tiny projected text can produce finite outputs but enormous gradients. Compute projection/normalization in FP32 with autocast disabled and a deliberate epsilon; `1e-12` underflows in FP16. Avoid zero-initializing a projection immediately before normalization. Mask missing fields before unsafe operations, normalize only valid rows, and explicitly zero their residuals afterward, including projection bias and padding. Multiplication by zero or `where` after invalid division cannot guarantee safe backward behavior. [PyTorch autograd guidance](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/autograd.html)

Preserving seed 42 alone does not preserve baseline initialization: additional module constructors consume random draws. Keep baseline construction and initialization order unchanged; isolate every added constructor and initialization pass inside `torch.random.fork_rng`, covering CPU and every touched CUDA device, or use explicit generators where supported. Python/NumPy randomness needs separate isolation. Verify baseline parameter equality and subsequent RNG states; a later recursive initializer can defeat constructor isolation. [PyTorch RNG documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.15/random.html)

Derived caching requirements: build the complete effective item table only after loading the selected checkpoint, calling `eval()`, and fixing device/dtype. Cache identity, detached current norms, trained projection/gates, masks, and padding consistently; use identical embeddings for history lookup and candidate scoring wherever training shares them. Invalidate after parameter updates, checkpoint loads, device/dtype changes, or metadata changes; never reuse detached caches during training. Compare cached/uncached scores and rankings, checking bitwise equality if required. `inference_mode()` does not disable dropout; `eval()` remains necessary. [PyTorch inference documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.autograd.grad_mode.inference_mode.html)
